Data was complete for all 672 quarter-hours in both series.

Source: Energy-Charts.info (Fraunhofer ISE), physical and scheduled commercial cross-border flows

installed_solar_vs_2030_target.question: How much solar capacity is installed in Germany, and what is the 2030 target?

content.text:
Germany had **120.98 GW of solar capacity installed at the end of November 2026** (latest monthly value), which is **120.98 GW AC (inverter)** or **133.00 GW DC (module)**. The legal 2030 target under EEG 2023 is **215 GW**. The source does not state whether that target is AC or DC, so I can't say which basis it uses. At the current level, about 94 GW would still need to be added by 2030 on the AC figure.

Source: Energy-Charts.info (Fraunhofer ISE), installed capacity (monthly and yearly series, including EEG 2023 targets).

hours_above_300_october.question: How many hours in October 2026 had a day-ahead price above 300 EUR/MWh?

solar_market_value_october.question: What was the market value (capture price) of solar power in October 2026, and how does it compare with the official value?

content.text:
In October 2026, the solar capture price in Germany was **13.45 ct/kWh (134.49 EUR/MWh)**, calculated from day-ahead prices weighted by public solar generation for 1–31 October. The official TSO value is **13.39 ct/kWh**, so the two differ by about 0.06 ct/kWh. That gap is expected, because the official figure uses the TSOs' extrapolated feed-in, while mine uses Energy-Charts generation data. The official October value is marked "reported" (published 10 November 2026), not final. For context, the simple average day-ahead price over the month was 169.27 EUR/MWh (16.93 ct/kWh), which matches the official spot average.

Source: Energy-Charts.info (Fraunhofer ISE); Bundesnetzagentur | SMARD.de (day-ahead prices); official monthly market value from netztransparenz.de (German TSOs), as reported by pv magazine and Solarserver

co2_factor_2025.question: What was the CO2 intensity of German electricity in 2025?

content.text:
The CO2 intensity of German electricity in 2025 was about **344 g CO2/kWh**, according to the Umweltbundesamt (UBA). This is an **estimate**, not a final figure. It is direct emissions from German generation divided by electricity consumed in Germany, and it excludes emissions from net imports.

Source: Umweltbundesamt (UBA), Climate Change 16/2026 (published 2026-03-23)

This is calculated from Energy-Charts' total net generation series, not an official weekly figure, and no official weekly renewable share is published to compare against.

official_renewable_share_2025.question: What was the official renewable share of German electricity generation in 2025?

content.text:
The official renewable share of gross electricity generation in Germany in 2025 was **57.9%**. This figure is **preliminary**, from BDEW based on AG Energiebilanzen data (published 8 December 2025). Gross generation includes power plants' own consumption and industrial generation, so the share is higher than the share of public net generation.

For comparison, the preliminary renewable share of gross electricity *consumption* for 2025 is **55.1%** (Umweltbundesamt). This is the basis of Germany's legal renewable targets.

Source: BDEW (based on AG Energiebilanzen), Stromerzeugung 2025; Umweltbundesamt, Erneuerbare Energien in Zahlen

Wind supplied **23.3%** of Germany's public net generation last week (Monday 2 to Sunday 8 November 2026). That is 2,098.7 GWh of wind out of 9,007.5 GWh total, with no missing data.

Public net generation is Energy-Charts' standard basis and excludes industrial self-supply. Official statistics have no weekly wind share to compare against, so this figure stands on its own.

Source: Energy-Charts.info (Fraunhofer ISE)

Solar supplied **7.8%** (7.75%) of Germany's public net generation last week (Monday 2 to Sunday 8 November 2026), which is 697.7 GWh out of 9,007.5 GWh total. That is roughly a third of wind's 23.3% share for the same week. The data is complete, with no missing values.

Source: Energy-Charts.info (Fraunhofer ISE)
